properties.natural_language: The RIPEMD-160 precompile must accept arbitrary-length input data (including zero-length) without error, as the hash function is defined for all byte sequences.
After RIPEMD-160 precompile execution completes successfully, the output (evm.output) must be exactly 32 bytes, consisting of 12 leading zero bytes followed by the 20-byte RIPEMD-160 digest.
The RIPEMD-160 hash function is deterministic: the same input bytes must always produce the same 20-byte digest regardless of call context, gas available, or caller identity.
The RIPEMD-160 precompile must always be available at address 0x03 and respond to CALL operations on mainnet and compatible chains.
Before RIPEMD-160 execution proceeds, the gas cost (GAS_RIPEMD160 base + GAS_RIPEMD160_WORD * ceil32(len(data))/32) must be deducted. If insufficient gas, the precompile must fail with out-of-gas.
After output format validation, the final output must be exactly 32 bytes where the first 12 bytes are zero and the last 20 bytes are the RIPEMD-160 digest.
The RIPEMD-160 digest is always exactly 160 bits (20 bytes), regardless of input size.
Call data provided by the transaction sender is entirely untrusted. CALLDATALOAD must use buffer_read to zero-pad out-of-bounds reads rather than returning garbage data.
Memory expansion gas must be calculated and charged before CALLDATACOPY writes to memory. Failure to charge gas first must result in out-of-gas, not a partial write.

For any environment opcode accessing external account state (BALANCE, EXTCODESIZE, EXTCODEHASH), a cold address access must charge GAS_COLD_ACCOUNT_ACCESS (2600) and add the address to accessed_addresses. A warm access must charge only GAS_WARM_ACCESS (100).
RETURNDATACOPY must validate that offset + size <= len(return_data) before any memory write. If bounds check fails, an OutOfBoundsRead exception must be raised, reverting execution.
After successful RETURNDATACOPY, the EVM memory at [dest_offset, dest_offset+size) must contain exactly the bytes from return_data[offset, offset+size).
Blob versioned hashes are provided by the transaction submitter and are untrusted. BLOBHASH must bounds-check the index: if index >= len(blob_versioned_hashes), return zero hash (not revert).

After BLOBHASH with a valid index, the stack must contain the exact 32-byte versioned hash from blob_versioned_hashes[index]. After BLOBHASH with an invalid index, the stack must contain exactly zero.
EXTCODEHASH must return zero for empty accounts (nonce=0, balance=0, no code) per EIP-161, and keccak256 of the code for non-empty accounts.
The BLAKE2b precompile input must be exactly 213 bytes. If input length differs, the precompile must fail (consume all provided gas and return failure).
The BLAKE2b final block flag (last byte of input) must be exactly 0 or 1. Any other value must cause the precompile to fail.
The BLAKE2b gas cost must equal rounds * 1 (GAS_PER_ROUND). The rounds value is extracted from the first 4 bytes of input as a big-endian uint32. Gas must be charged before execution begins.

The BLAKE2b G-function must perform all 8 operations (4 add-xor-rotate pairs) in the exact order specified by RFC 7693. Each arithmetic operation must be performed modulo 2^64 using mask 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF.

The BLAKE2b compression function must execute exactly the number of rounds specified in the input. The round counter must increment by 1 per iteration and terminate when it reaches the specified count.
After all compression rounds complete, the output must be the 64-byte little-endian encoding of the final state vector h[0..7] XORed with the upper and lower halves of the work vector.
For Gray Glacier difficulty calculation, the bomb delay offset must be exactly 11,400,000 blocks. The fake_block_number must be computed as max(0, actual_block_number - 11,400,000).

The difficulty bomb exponential component must equal 2^((fake_block_number // 100000) - 2). This must be added to the Homestead adjustment component. The final difficulty must never be less than the minimum difficulty.
Blocks received from the P2P network must have their difficulty validated against the expected Gray Glacier calculation. Blocks with incorrect difficulty must be rejected.
Blocks received from P2P must pass Proof of Work verification: the block hash must be less than or equal to 2^256 / difficulty. Invalid PoW must cause block rejection.

After block state transition, the post-block state must reflect all transaction executions in order, followed by mining rewards (2 ETH base + uncle rewards). The state root must match the Merkle Patricia Trie root of the final state.
EIP-5069 is a Meta EIP defining governance processes. It has no protocol-runtime security properties. Editor admission/rejection does not affect on-chain consensus or state transitions.

Before SSTORE can execute, gasleft must be strictly greater than 2300. If gasleft <= 2300 (i.e., only the call stipend remains), SSTORE must throw an out-of-gas exception to prevent reentrancy attacks.
The gas stipend boundary check for SSTORE must use strict greater-than (gasleft > 2300), not greater-than-or-equal. The value 2300 itself must trigger failure.

For SSTORE gas metering, the three-value tracking invariant must hold: original value (pre-transaction) is immutable within a transaction, current value reflects the latest write, and new value is the proposed write.
When current == new (no-op write), SSTORE must charge exactly SLOAD_GAS (800 gas). No state change occurs and no refund is modified.
When original == current (clean slot) and original == 0, SSTORE must charge SSTORE_SET_GAS (20000). When original == current and original != 0, SSTORE must charge SSTORE_RESET_GAS (5000).
When original != current (dirty slot), SSTORE must charge only SLOAD_GAS (800) regardless of the new value.
When a clean slot is cleared to zero (original != 0, current == original, new == 0), SSTORE_CLEARS_SCHEDULE (15000) must be added to the refund counter.

When a dirty slot is restored to its original value (new == original, current != original), an appropriate refund must be added. When a dirty slot is un-zeroed (current == 0, new != 0), SSTORE_CLEARS_SCHEDULE must be removed from the refund counter.

A storage slot within a single transaction can only be in one of four states: untouched, zeroed, modified (non-zero different from original), or restored (equal to original). Transitions between these states must follow the defined state machine.
The gas refund counter at transaction completion must be capped at 50% of total gas consumed. This prevents gas refund manipulation attacks.
For Constantinople and later blocks, the fake_block_number must be computed as max(0, block.number - 5,000,000). Pre-Constantinople blocks must use the actual block number for difficulty calculation.
The difficulty formula must produce deterministic results: for a given parent header and block number, the expected difficulty is uniquely determined. No randomness or non-determinism is allowed.

Post-Constantinople, the base block reward must be exactly 2 ETH (2,000,000,000,000,000,000 wei). Nephew reward must be base_reward / 32 per included uncle. Uncle reward must be ((8 - k) * base_reward) / 8 where k is the uncle age.
After reward computation, the coinbase account balance must increase by exactly the sum of base reward plus nephew rewards. Uncle miner accounts must each increase by their respective uncle reward.
Blocks received from peers must have their difficulty validated against the expected calculation (including correct fork rules and bomb delay). Blocks with mismatched difficulty must be rejected.

After difficulty validation passes, blocks must also have their reward application verified: the state transition must include exactly the correct reward credits. Incorrect rewards must cause block rejection.
After the Deneb fork upgrade, the beacon state must contain all Capella fields unchanged, plus blob_gas_used initialized to 0 and excess_blob_gas initialized to 0 in the ExecutionPayloadHeader.

During the Deneb fork upgrade, all pre-existing Capella beacon state fields (genesis_time, validators, balances, slashings, participation flags, sync committees, etc.) must be preserved exactly without any modification.

The fork version chain must be maintained: after Deneb upgrade, previous_version must equal CAPELLA_FORK_VERSION and current_version must equal DENEB_FORK_VERSION. The fork epoch must be correctly set.
After Deneb fork upgrade, blob_gas_used and excess_blob_gas must both be initialized to exactly uint64(0). These fields enable the EIP-4844 blob gas fee market.
EIP-7702 Authorization chain_id must either match the current chain ID or be zero (wildcard). Any other value must cause the authorization to be rejected.
EIP-7702 Authorization ECDSA signature (y_parity, r, s) must be valid and recoverable to an authority address. Invalid signatures must cause authorization rejection without side effects.

External byte data entering the system must pass type length validation: Address must be exactly 20 bytes, Root must be exactly 32 bytes, Bloom must be exactly 256 bytes. Data failing these checks must be rejected.

The EMPTY_ACCOUNT constant (nonce=0, balance=0, code=b'') must be the canonical representation of non-existent accounts. Account encoding via RLP must always include nonce, balance, storage_root, and keccak256(code).
The storage_root used in account encoding must be a valid Merkle Patricia Trie root. Corrupted storage roots would compromise state integrity.
Messages received from the wallet provider via postMessage must have their origin validated before processing. Messages from untrusted origins must be discarded.
Wallet discovery messages received via web+evm:// protocol handler must be validated. The initial message must contain a MessagePort for establishing the primary communication channel.
Wallet response messages must have exactly one of 'result' or 'error' fields. Messages with both or neither must be treated as protocol errors and rejected.
ProviderInfo received from wallet must be validated for required fields (name, icon). The icon URI must be sanitized before rendering to prevent XSS attacks via malicious SVG or javascript: URIs.
The first MessagePort received during wallet discovery must be stored as the primary port. All subsequent RPC requests must use this primary port for communication consistency.
The wallet discovery iframe must use src='web+evm://' and be properly attached to the DOM. The listener must be registered before the iframe is attached to avoid race conditions.
Nodes syncing past the Deneb fork epoch must apply the upgrade_to_deneb function at the correct slot during sync, producing the same state as nodes that were online at fork time.
Authorization nonce (U64) must be compared correctly against account nonce (Uint) despite potential type differences. The comparison must be unsigned integer equality.
RIPEMD-160 gas cost must be exactly GAS_RIPEMD160 (600) + GAS_RIPEMD160_WORD (120) * ceil32(len(data)) / 32. The word count formula must use ceiling division to 32-byte boundaries.

Gray Glacier is the final PoW difficulty adjustment before The Merge. No further difficulty bomb delays should be expected. The 11.4M block offset must remain constant for all blocks in the Gray Glacier era.

Existing contracts that relied on implicit reentrancy protection from high SSTORE gas costs must remain protected under EIP-2200. The gas stipend check (gasleft > 2300) specifically maintains this invariant.

BLAKE2b work vector initialization must combine state vector h[0..7] with initialization vector IV[0..7]. Offset counters must be XORed into positions v[12] and v[13]. If final flag is set, v[14] must have all bits inverted.
BLAKE2b rotation constants must be exactly: R1=32, R2=24, R3=16, R4=63 for BLAKE2b. Using incorrect rotation values would produce wrong hash outputs.
If the RIPEMD-160 hashlib implementation encounters a failure, it must be treated as an EVM execution error. The precompile must not return partial or incorrect results.
EIP-2200 gas metering rules apply to all SSTORE operations regardless of execution context (normal transaction, internal call, or CREATE/CREATE2).
